anomalies.observed: J7 (AVR-ISP-6) pin 3 (SCK) is wired to net NET0003, which is the ATtiny PB3 pin (U7 pin 2, U2 pin 2).
anomalies.expected: On ATtiny13/45/85 the ISP SCK must be PB2 (net NET0002); PB3 is not the ISP clock pin.

evidence.quote: J7 AVR-ISP-6: SCK (pin 3) -> NET0003; U7 ATtiny45-20P: XTAL1/PB3 (pin 2) -> NET0003

anomalies.impact: In-system programming via J7 would fail because the programmer's SCK would toggle PB3 instead of PB2.

anomalies.observed: J6 (POT) pin 2 (wiper) is wired to net NET0012, which is the ATtiny PB5/RESET pin (U7 pin 1, U2 pin 1), and R4 (1K) pulls this same net up to +5V.
anomalies.expected: A potentiometer wiper should feed an ADC input (PB2/PB3/PB4), not the RESET pin.

evidence.quote: J6 POT: pin 2 -> NET0012; U7 ATtiny45-20P: RESET/PB5 (pin 1) -> NET0012; R4 1K between +5V and NET0012

anomalies.impact: The pot cannot be read as an analog input and it loads the RESET line, preventing the programmer from resetting the ATtiny during ISP.

parsed.summary: The schematic appears to miswire the ATtiny ISP clock (SCK to PB3 instead of PB2) and the potentiometer wiper (to PB5/RESET instead of an ADC pin), either of which would break programming and fan-speed control.
